title: GH#22354: refactor setup into focused modules below 1200 lines
body:
## Summary

Continue the earlier merged split after `setup.sh` regrew to 2,232 lines. Move
34 functions verbatim into three focused, guarded modules. Preserve bootstrap,
entrypoint-relative paths, lock ownership and completion in the public entrypoint.

Resolves #22354

| File | Lines | Responsibility |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `setup.sh` | 1191 | Bootstrap, globals, CLI parser, mutex, timing, runtime reconciliation, completion |
| `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/setup-interface.sh` | 252 | Stage names/help, desktop opt-in, upgrade/config helpers |
| `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/setup-execution.sh` | 746 | Incremental plans, scoped/interactive/non-interactive stages, schedulers |
| `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/setup-postflight.sh` | 76 | Post-deploy dispatch and final interactive instructions |

Canonical module placement preserves the existing incremental planner's full-setup
invalidation for implementation changes. Keep `parse_args` and `_setup_print_header`
in place to preserve the local hook's positional/literal debt identities, without
rewrites or hook bypasses. Eight existing test loaders now follow the moved code;
their behavioral assertions remain intact.

## Testing

- All four production shell files pass `bash -n`, `shfmt -d`, and `git diff --check`.
- `bash setup.sh --help` passes.
- Initial `affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base --max 60`: four
  suites pass; scoped-dispatch and source-access-broker are inherited red
  (`rc_head=1 rc_base=1`), zero regressions, zero omitted suites. The former lacks
  native ShellCheck on this runner; the latter fails at the unchanged signed-tag
  fixture at line 135 before reaching the adapted assertions.
- Existing setup mutex, timing (2), complexity-scan (4), OpenCode V2, lock (13)
  and completion-sentinel suites pass. Scoped-dispatch's other 60 assertions pass.
- CI identified two additional static readers. After redirecting their source
  locations, Vault runtime readiness passes 20/20 and Pulse standalone passes
  37/37. Assertions and production behavior are unchanged. Concurrent repair
  commits are preserved; the reconciliation tree exactly matches their final tree.
- All four complexity metrics report `new=0`; no override label is needed.
- Native ShellCheck is unavailable behind the local wrapper. The PR's
  `Code Quality Analysis / ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` job supplies that gate.
- `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` has pre-existing shfmt differences outside changed
  lines; no unrelated formatting changes included.

### Pure-move evidence

`python3 .agents/scripts/file-split-verify.py --base e3ba746036 --head f917933ac3`

is pinned so this evidence remains reproducible after merge):

```text

```

The final range intentionally reports `removed-only=15 review=30`, entirely in
the eight existing test loaders. Exact intentional locations:

- `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh:299-302`: four call-site searches use the execution module.
- `test-setup-cli-convergence-mutex.sh:10,39-44`: module variable and deployment/CLI searches.
- `test-setup-noninteractive-complexity-scan.sh:10`: scheduler source location.
- `test-setup-scoped-dispatch.sh:18,99-110,211`: verify the entrypoint sources all three modules, combine module text for static assertions, and extract the relocated checkout helper.

- `test-setup-stage-timing-observability.sh:9,81`: extract the relocated non-interactive stage.
- `test-vault-runtime-readiness.sh:99`: inspect the relocated Vault setup call.
- `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh:73,327`: inspect the relocated scheduler gate/call while retaining the entrypoint existence check.

These are test integration, not production logic changes. Two non-failing warnings

title: t19309: fix(headless): release the dispatch claim before the exit-trap terminal lease
body:
## Summary

_hrff_finalize_exit_trap emitted the worker runtime event before releasing the claim. Since GH#36553 that event posts this attempt's DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal, and dispatch-release-claim.jq then returns verdict terminal, so the following release was skipped ("no current unreleased matching dispatch claim"). Every prelaunch failure that exits through the EXIT trap (e.g. project_node_environment_failure) therefore left the issue assigned with status:in-progress until a peer's stale sweep reset it 12-30 min later, and two such resets trip the t2008 escalation to status:blocked + needs-ai-recovery. Observed 2026-11-23 on a private downstream repo: one device failed 33/33 dispatches in ~4 s each, posting only terminal leases and never CLAIM_RELEASED; five healthy issues were escalated within 30 minutes. The release now runs first (as _hrw_finish_not_launched and the normal finish path already do), so CLAIM_RELEASED with the prelaunch cause publishes and projects state immediately; the event's terminal lease remains the fallback. Dedup is unaffected: dispatch-lease-claims.jq maps a matching CLAIM_RELEASED to terminal attempt_id release, which _dd_has_matching_terminal_lease accepts. Also points a stale test assertion at headless-runtime-failure-classify.sh, where GH#37744 moved classify_worker_kill_reason (it failed on main).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19309-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — shellcheck clean on both scripts. PASS: test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh, test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh, test-worker-exit-classifier.sh, test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh, test-project-node-runtime.sh, test-runtime-events-cli.sh; test-worker-exited-kill-reason.sh 27/27 after the assertion path fix (26/27 on main, pre-existing). Code-path verification: dispatch-release-claim.jq:49-50 returns terminal once a bound terminal lease follows the claim; headless-runtime-release-claim.sh:67-68 skips on that verdict; dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:931 accepts attempt_id release. Production confirmation pending the next prelaunch failure on an updated runner.

Resolves #40008

title: GH#40028: fix(quality-sweep): report unavailable ShellCheck as skipped instead of All clear
body:
## Summary

_sweep_shellcheck now probes the analyser by running `shellcheck --version`, so a wrapper or shim with no real binary fails the probe; `command -v` only checked that a command existed. A failed probe returns 127, so the existing caller lists `ShellCheck (rc=127)` under Skipped tools and emits no section. Each file is classified by exit code and output: it counts as analysed only for rc 0 with no output, or rc 1 with gcc-format findings. Timeouts, rc>=2, wrapper errors and the wrapper's rate-limit JSON are logged and counted as not analysed, never rendered as findings. title: GH#40026: fix(gh-wrappers): require a declaration for closing keywords in PR body prose
body:
## Summary

GitHub closes the target of a closing keyword anywhere in a PR body, including conditional or explanatory prose such as `would make the sync close #N`. The previous guard only matched negated phrasings, an open-ended wordlist. This PR adds `_gh_pr_body_undeclared_closing_ref` in `gh-closing-reference-lib.sh`, which enforces a positive invariant: a closing keyword counts as a declaration only when it starts a line, list item or sentence, or continues a declaration list (`Resolves #1, fixes #2`). Any other closing reference must name a target that also has a declaration. Code spans and fenced blocks are ignored, and qualified self-repo references normalise to `#N`. `_gh_validate_pr_closing_keywords` (create, edit, shim, merge --body) rejects undeclared prose. `_gh_pr_merge_closure_check` (full-loop and Pulse merge) holds the same bodies. `gh-command-discipline.md` documents the rule.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md, .agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-edit-safety.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-closing-contradiction.sh

## Decisions

A positive declaration invariant replaces another wordlist extension. Prose mentions of a declared target stay allowed, so a body that both declares and discusses the same issue is not rejected. Issue bodies and comments remain out of scope because GitHub only acts on closing keywords in PR bodies and commit messages.

## Summary

Stale recovery counted every reset toward the t2008 threshold (2), so one runner whose launch path failed (claim posted, no DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready) escalated healthy issues to status:blocked + needs-ai-recovery after two of its own failures, though the issue itself was never attempted. Such resets write <!-- stale-recovery-tick:launch-failure runner=LOGIN --> instead of a numeric tick. The shared tick-state jq counts numeric ticks each and launch-failure ticks once per runner, so a second failure by the same runner does not escalate, while failures on two runners (or a launch failure plus an ordinary stale) still reach the threshold. Maintainer release markers reset both; a merged-PR progress marker restarts at its own tick; latest-tick timestamps include launch-failure ticks. title: GH#40059: fix(ci-wait): zero-check PRs return terminal no-checks instead of hanging
body:
## Summary

GitHub returns commit.statusCheckRollup: null when a head has no check runs or statuses. The exact reader (_gh_pr_checks_exact_page_meta) rejected that as a partial/malformed page, so gh-checks-wait-helper retried until its 1800s timeout in both required and --all modes. The reader now accepts a null rollup on page 1 as a complete empty page (a rollup lost after page 1 stays fail-closed as partial). The waiter's fetch_checks now maps the mode-matched empty diagnostic ('no checks reported...' for --all, the existing required form otherwise) to []. Because an empty --all read can now reach classification, it holds the existing 90s settle window unless the repo is verified to have zero active workflows, so a fresh head cannot pass before its workflows register. The existing zero-check fixture now uses GitHub's real null shape. A second commit extracts reset_wait_caches/resolve_classification_evidence so wait_for_checks stays under the 100-line complexity gate.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-pr-checks-exact-json.sh

## Decisions

Fixed at the shared reader (root cause) instead of special-casing mergeStateStatus or raising timeouts. Added the active-workflow gate for empty --all reads so the newly reachable no-checks PASS cannot race workflow registration; unknown/malformed workflow evidence falls back to the settle window (fail-safe). Rollup state is the middle TSV field because bash read collapses consecutive tabs before an empty trailing cursor. jq type checks use arrays/numbers selectors to satisfy the string-literal ratchet.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime, patched worktree helper against live PRs: octocat/git-consortium#123 (0 workflows) --all -> 'PASS: verified no checks reported in 6s'; octocat/Hello-World#11781 (2 active workflows) required -> 'PASS: verified no required checks ... in 96s' (settle window), --all with settle=15 -> 'PASS: verified no checks reported in 19s'. Baseline deployed helper on the same PR -> 'INDETERMINATE: required-check state unavailable after 47s' (the reported retry loop). Live GraphQL confirms octocat/Hello-World@master statusCheckRollup is null. Workflow-count jq filter re-verified live: git-consortium -> 0, Hello-World -> 2, null input -> malformed error. Checks: shellcheck clean on all 3 files; test-gh-pr-checks-exact-json.sh 87/87 (incl. new required-mode null-rollup assertion); test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh 132/132 after the refactor; affected-tests-helper --compare-base: 27 pass, 0 regressions, 3 pre-existing reds identical on base (null-suites, issue-sync-git-push-helper timeout, circuit-breaker-investigation-task XDG_RUNTIME_DIR unbound) tracked separately.

## Summary

A commit-and-pr validator TIMEOUT (exit 124) no longer blocks PR creation when the PR base branch already requires a status check for the same phase (format/lint/typecheck/test). The lookup unions rulesets and classic protection once per run and fails closed on any API or parse failure. Later phases in the same scope that CI also requires are deferred, phases CI does not require still run locally, and non-timeout failures and the check-only mutation guard are unchanged. Each deferral is printed and appended to the PR Runtime Testing line; the required check still gates merge.

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh, .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-project-validators-shell-only.sh

Not chosen: raising the default timeout (pushes finished work further into the worker hard cap and adds load to a saturated host) or skipping local validators (they still run and still block on real failures). title: GH#40058: fix(repo-layout): part A - migrate-layout tolerates prunable worktrees; audited prune-missing-worktrees
body:
## Summary

Part A of #40058 (part B, outside-workspace sources, follows separately). (1) repo_layout_repository.py: new prunable_worktree_paths() returns linked registrations Git marks `prunable` whose path is absent; linked_pointer_records skips only those, so every other missing/unexpected pointer stays fail-closed. repo_layout_migrate.py records them in a new per-repository plan field `prunable_worktrees`, and validate_repository_plan fails as drift if any reappears. (2) canonical-recovery-helper.sh prune-missing-worktrees --repo PATH [--issue N] --confirm PRUNE_MISSING_WORKTREES: verifies the audit chain, writes an operation.verify record, then reuses the existing prune_missing_worktree_metadata primitive per absent entry and verifies each is gone; no new prune implementation and no canonical-guard exception. The canonical Git guard's 'git worktree' block message now names this route. (3) The selector moved from cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh into audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh (missing_worktree_prune_targets) so async cleanup and the recovery command share one guard; the unmounted-volume deferral no longer applies when the absent parent is under a fixed system temp root (/tmp, /private/tmp, /var/tmp, /var/folders and /private variants; $TMPDIR deliberately not trusted). (4) reference/repo-organization.md Migration safety documents both.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/repo-organization.md, .agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py, .agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py, .agents/scripts/repo_layout_repository.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh, tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py

## Decisions

Reused the audited prune primitive rather than adding a guard exception (the review's explicit constraint). Prune is repo-wide in native Git, so the recovery command refuses the whole repo when any absent entry is in the unmounted-volume shape, matching async cleanup. Temp roots are a fixed list; trusting $TMPDIR would let an env var widen the exception. Compatibility symlinks remain declined per Migration safety.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime fixture (real git repo, native git): worktree under /private/tmp with parent wiped -> prune-missing-worktrees prints PRUNED + PRUNED_MISSING_WORKTREES=1, registration gone, 1 audit record; wrong --confirm -> 'BLOCKED: exact recovery confirmation is required'; worktree whose parent is absent outside temp (unmounted-volume shape) -> BLOCKED, registration retained. tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py: new test_prunable_worktree_is_recorded_and_survives_apply_rollback (plan records prunable path; reappearing path refuses apply; apply + rollback restore exact snapshot) plus 17 existing = 18/18 (run with AIDEVOPS_TABBY_PYTHON_ENV; the tabby interpreter case passes under a PyYAML interpreter, environment-only). test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh 47/47 (stub now supplies the shared selector); test-worktree-metadata-prune.sh exit 0 (pre-existing false-pass filed as #40071); test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh 216/216; shellcheck clean; py_compile clean.; macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at d2f33ebd4bb58420f803c71f86cad6106f8ded11.

title: GH#40058: fix(repo-layout): part B - migrate-layout accepts registered outside-workspace and nested sources
body:
## Summary

Part B of #40058 (part A merged in #40078). (1) select_plan_sources: with --include-registered-paths, a --source that discovery does not report (outside the workspace, or nested in another repository) is accepted only via repo_layout_repository.validate_registered_source: exact repos.json initialized_repos[].path match, not local_only, does not contain the workspace, own .git directory and rev-parse toplevel == source (refuses linked worktrees and modern submodules), and not a 160000 gitlink in an enclosing repository. Without the flag the original refusal message is unchanged; discovery-only plans are untouched. (2) Nested selections: nested_first_order puts every nested source before each selected source containing it, so apply moves the child out first and the existing reversed rollback restores the parent before the child. The parent records nested_sources and its fingerprint (status, untracked digest, main worktree record) omits those paths via :(exclude,literal) pathspecs, which validate/move/rollback recompute identically; with no exclusions the Git invocations are byte-identical to before, so existing plan digests still verify. validate_nested_moves refuses a plan when a nested selection has no planned move or would land inside its parent. Cross-device refusal is unchanged. (3) reference/repo-organization.md Migration safety documents the outside-workspace --source rule and nested ordering.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/repo-organization.md, .agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py, .agents/scripts/repo_layout_repository.py, tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py

## Decisions

Exclusion is applied only to the parent's own working-tree state, not diffs or refs, because the nested repo is untracked content from the parent's view. Empty exclusions keep the historical Git argv so old plans verify. A nested child destination inside its parent is refused rather than reordered. Registration matching stays lexical (expand_path), consistent with plan_repository, so a symlinked spelling is refused rather than guessed. Compatibility symlinks remain declined per Migration safety.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py 20/20 under the Tabby PyYAML interpreter (AIDEVOPS_TABBY_PYTHON_ENV set). New test_registered_outside_and_nested_sources_round_trip is the review's fixture: registered Hub in a projects directory outside the workspace, registered Nested untracked inside Hub, and a Hub linked worktree whose temp parent was wiped (prunable). plan orders [Nested, Hub], records nested_sources and prunable_worktrees and is non-mutating; apply moves both into the workspace owner directory and retargets repos.json; status=applied; rollback restores the original projects tree byte-for-byte (sha256 over every path and file) and the repos.json bytes. New test_unapproved_or_unsafe_outside_sources_are_refused: unflagged, unregistered, local_only, linked-worktree and workspace-containing sources are each refused with no plan written. py_compile clean.

Resolves #40058

body:
## Summary

Resolves #40081.

- Retry scoped headless gopass timeouts once with twice the configured bound (maximum 55 seconds per attempt).
- Preserve exit 5 through scoped injection and report the final timeout and load rather than suggesting the store is locked. Actual gopass failures retain exit 1 and are not retried.
- Keep status-only secret checks single-attempt; document behavior and extend the existing regression suite.

## Files and reference pattern

Changes stay within the four-file Files Scope: .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/secret-redaction-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh, and .agents/reference/secret-handling.md. Reuses the existing Python process-group supervisor and fail-closed environment construction.

## Verification

All 56 secret-helper assertions pass. Affected-suite comparison selected seven suites with none omitted: five passed; test-encryption-git-roundtrip.sh and test-terminal-output-contract.sh fail identically on head and origin/main (pre-existing, not repaired in this PR). Bash syntax and git diff checks passed. Independent read-only review found no actionable defects. Local ShellCheck wrapper cannot locate its real binary; CI ShellCheck must cover it. The repository push hook defers TypeScript checking to CI because tsc is unavailable locally.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — all 56 production-path secret-helper assertions passed at 84d52227bb279fb5f21c9744001a941dd5fe5fd0 using isolated gopass stubs
- **Verified HEAD:** 84d52227bb279fb5f21c9744001a941dd5fe5fd0

Isolated gopass stubs exercise the production scoped injection command: a slow first attempt followed by a 1.3s second attempt succeeds under the doubled 2s bound; persistent slow reads return 5 with the timeout/load diagnostic without running the child; immediate non-zero gopass exits return 1 without retry. title: GH#40087: fix(buzz): bound ACP turns and delegate proxy runtime to the plugin
body:
## Summary

The Buzz plugin now enforces its declared 30-minute turn limit: an overdue session/prompt is cancelled via session/cancel, and if OpenCode has not ended it 60 s later the agent's ACP process is stopped and its sessions forgotten, so the queue moves on with a clear failure reply. With turns bounded, process-guard delegates runtime for the exact deployed `team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs --no-publish -- .../opencode-launcher-helper.sh remote-interactive` command line and its `opencode acp` child (owner `buzz-acp-plugin`). Arbitrary Node/OpenCode processes stay governed; RSS limits remain enforced. Plugin version 1.3.1.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/README.md, .agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js, .agents/scripts/process-guard-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-process-guard-managed-workers.sh

## Decisions

Skipped the optional proxy signal rewording: the plugin's own acp.stop() also SIGTERMs the proxy, so attributing SIGTERM to a process guard would mislead. Local Node project validators were skipped (AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1) because they refuse any .agents/**/*.js change: .agents/package.json is a scriptless dependency manifest outside the root workspaces, so no package check owns plugin.js. No check that could run was skipped; CI gates apply. Follow-up issue filed for the validator gap.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Live: real Node processes with the exact proxy argv and a lookalike without --no-publish, scanned by this branch's process-guard-helper.sh scan with CHILD_RUNTIME_LIMIT=1: proxy => MANAGED 'runtime delegated to buzz-acp-plugin lifecycle controls'; lookalike => OVER_TIME. Plugin: harness loading plugin.js's own boundedTurn source with shortened limits: stalled prompt sends session/cancel, then stops and forgets the ACP process and rejects within timeout+grace; an overdue turn ending as cancelled rejects without a stop; normal answers pass through with no cancel. bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-process-guard-managed-workers.sh 75/75 (proxy, acp child, npm wrapper hop MANAGED; filename-in-args, missing --no-publish, orphan acp, non-acp child, non-proxy parent stay OVER; kill path skips old proxy; over-RSS proxy still killed). shellcheck clean; node --check plugin.js ok. Not run: a >2h live Buzz soak.

Resolves #40087

body:
## Summary

Shell Suite Main Health now provisions the managed Vault crypto runtime at ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/python-env/vault with the production setup_vault_python_env function and the pinned .agents/configs/vault-requirements.txt, right after the existing framework staging. Vault helpers trust only that managed runtime, so test-vault-helper.sh and test-vault-setup-flow.sh were exercising a missing installation in the health job. The step fails closed on an existing destination and verifies with vault-runtime-check.py. No setup.sh, no services; storm bound 10 and artifact reporting unchanged. Assessment of the remaining red rows from runs 45235432789 and 45264398128: about 60 reproduce on a maintainer macOS host at current main and are genuine drift owned by #40041; 9 depend on maintainer HOME state such as the privacy repos.json inventory and need hermetic fixtures, not a workflow change, per the #40039 precedent; the rest are Linux-specific per-suite behaviour. The full row map is posted on the issue.



## Files Changed

.github/workflows/shell-suite-main-health.yml

## Decisions

Call the production setup_vault_python_env instead of duplicating its ownership and marker sequence inline, so the CI runtime cannot drift from what setup provisions. Do not seed a global privacy inventory: #40039 established per-fixture synthetic inventories as the contract. Keep #40029 open with For, not Resolves, because remaining rows exceed the storm bound and are tracked by #40041.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — actionlint clean, including shellcheck of run blocks; bash -n passes for all 5 run blocks. Linux reproduction in ubuntu:24.04 as an unprivileged user with a 750 HOME, running the new step body under bash -e: runtime provisioned with cryptography 50.0.0, cffi 2.1.0 and pycparser 3.0; vault-runtime-check passes; a second run refuses replacement. test-vault-helper.sh and test-vault-setup-flow.sh pass there, while both are red in health runs 45235432789 and 45264398128 and under a disposable macOS HOME. test-vault-runtime-readiness.sh still passes. test-vault-audit-helper.sh and test-vault-sync-helper.sh stay red because they call system python3 with cryptography directly, which is fixture drift issue #40041.

## Regression Evidence

## Summary

Adds an executable read-only Pulse throughput CLI with ISO windows (default last 24 hours), text and JSON output, and graceful missing-log handling (`n/a` / `null`).

- Handles changing observed ceremony caps. Untimestamped round headers use the preceding log timestamp; coverage is exposed rather than inventing a cap.

title: t19325: fix(dispatch): size worker prelaunch lease to cover the canary bound
body:
## Summary

Pulse workers lost their dispatch lease when the model canary ran a real probe for longer than about 110 seconds, and then exited with `worker_ledger_ready_failed`. That is what happened to GH#40112's first attempt.

- The worker renewed its prelaunch claim for 120 s, but the canary that follows is bounded by `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (180 s). The ready transitions reject expired leases on both the GitHub claim and the local ledger, by design.
- The renewal did not extend `dispatch-ledger.jsonl` at all. The dispatcher's registration used the default 120 s prelaunch TTL.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-ownership.sh`: the new `_hrw_prelaunch_lease_ttl` returns the larger of the orphan grace and `CANARY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` + `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PRELAUNCH_ALLOWANCE_SECONDS`, which is 300 s by default. The renewal passes it to the GitHub claim transition, then makes a best-effort ledger renewal with the same TTL. This follows manual dispatch, which already sizes its lease from the canary timeout (`_dsi_renew_prelaunch_lease`).
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`: new `renew` command. It extends only an active `prelaunch` lease for the matching token, never shortens it, never turns a `ready` lease back into `prelaunch`, and never revives an expired lease. The strict expiry checks on `ready` are unchanged.

## Evidence

- GH#40112 attempt `attempt:789867d0`: the ledger lease expired at 00:20:40Z; the canary ran from 00:18:51Z to 00:21:24Z (153 s); `ready` ran at about 00:21:35Z, giving `worker_ledger_ready_failed`.
- Across 1,182 retained worker logs, the renewal-to-ready gap has a median of 7 s and a p90 of 13 s, with a maximum of 165 s (this attempt). It is rare, but it clusters when providers are slow.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` is clean on both files, and the pre-commit ratchets pass.
- An ad-hoc runtime check against a temporary ledger passed 12 of 12 cases: extends, keeps prelaunch, a shorter renewal is a no-op that appends nothing, a wrong token is denied, ready follows renewal, a ready lease cannot be downgraded, an expired lease is not revived, a missing entry is denied.
- `_hrw_prelaunch_lease_ttl`: default 300 s; 162 s with a 42 s canary; falls back on invalid input; never drops below the orphan-grace floor.
- Existing suites pass: `tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-atomic-lease.sh`, `tests/test-worker-warm-start-opencode.sh`.

## Cost

A worker that dies during prelaunch holds its dedup lease for up to 300 s instead of 120 s.

Resolves #40118

title: t19324: runner-local dispatch lock behind PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT
body:
## Summary

Adds a runner-local dispatch lock (LOCKDIR.dispatch, override PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCKDIR) separate from the Pulse instance lock, behind PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT (default 0). With the flag on, every dispatch round (early_dispatch, post_label_refill, cycle_dispatch_max, active-pulse refill, early_exit_recycle_fill, cycle_final_refill, event_refill_drain) takes the dispatch lock, so rounds never overlap, and a refill-only run no longer waits for the instance lock held through maintenance stages. Each acquire logs the owner PID (BASHPID-resolved, so subshell rounds record their real PID). Stale reclaim covers a dead owner, PID reuse by a non-pulse command, and a heartbeat older than PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S; the instance-lock heartbeat also refreshes the dispatch heartbeat. The lock is re-entrant, release is owner-checked, and it is released on EXIT before the instance lock and before the exec path. Refill-only runs without the env var follow the mode published by the latest cycle (LOCKDIR.dispatch-mode). With the flag off, nothing changes: every wrapper falls through to a direct call, and refill keeps the instance lock, the GH#35349 cooldown and the refill budget. Old refill layers are kept (Phase 3 follow-up). Rollout: merge with the flag off; enable on one runner via its launchd/systemd environment and compare pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh output (#40109) for 6 h before and after; making it the default is a follow-up.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh

## Decisions

Shared-state audit (flag on). (1) Candidate census and handoff: MOVED. Invalidation in post_label_refill, Phase 2 consolidation and triage enumeration runs inside dispatch rounds, and the refill census hand-off runs under the dispatch lock. Cycle EXIT cleanup still runs outside it but is SAFE: the hand-off is mktemp+mv atomic, removals only force a re-scan, and live claim/ledger gates still arbitrate every candidate. (2) Worktree cleanup vs dedup precreate_worktree: SAFE. The owner PID is recorded at precreate (pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh), cleanup checks _worktree_owner_alive, and orphans get a 1800 s grace. (3) cleanup_stale_opencode vs a just-spawned worker: SAFE. It prunes caches and scratch only and never kills workers (pulse-cleanup.sh). (4) Ownership and assignment reconcile: SAFE. _preflight_ownership_reconcile writes no ledger, PID or claim files. dispatch-ledger cmd_expire holds the ledger lock and expires only dead-PID, PID-reuse or lease-expired entries, while in-flight prelaunch claims renew their lease. stale_queued_runs only cancels queued GitHub Actions runs. normalize_active_issue_assignments keeps its existing 600 s updatedAt guard on unassign. (5) Slot accounting: MOVED. Throttle-file writers and base-parallel compute run inside apply_dispatch_max rounds, now serialized; active-worker counts read live processes. (6) Stats read-modify-write: SAFE. pulse_stats_increment serializes on its own stats lock with temp+mv writes. The two-live-workers-per-issue guarantee still rests on the existing dispatch claim/ledger dedup, which this change does not weaken; with the flag on, rounds no longer overlap at all.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Acceptance suites pass on the rebased branch: test-pulse-event-refill (39/39), test-dispatch-max-parallel, test-pulse-cycle-state-contract, test-pulse-wrapper-characterization (54/54), test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape. Adjacent suites pass: test-permission-block-breaker (42 cases; the extracted-pipeline harness needed the guarded _pulse_pipeline_dispatch_round fallback added here), pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring, pulse-dispatch-first-wave, pulse-merge-first-nonblocking, pulse-lock-force-reclaim (37/37), pulse-wrapper-worker-detection (40/40), dispatch-min-concurrency (36/36), pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot, pulse-watchdog-tick. test-pulse-singleton-lock case 4 and test-pulse-instance-lock-mkdir-only (live owner, 2 cases) fail identically on an unmodified git archive of origin/main on this host, so they predate this change. Real entry point (pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only, sandboxed HOME, no GitHub token, live pulse-wrapper instance lock holder): flag off gives action=lock_busy lock=instance with the trigger retained (current behaviour); flag on logs Dispatch lock acquired owner_pid=N stage=event_refill_drain, the instance lock stays untouched and no dispatch lock is left behind. A throwaway flag-on harness covered drain_started under a held instance lock, no overlap when the dispatch lock is busy (trigger retained), stage skip, stale-heartbeat and killed-subshell reclaim, nesting, child heartbeat refresh, and mode file on/off. ShellCheck: only the pre-existing SC2119/SC2120 on dispatch_max (identical on the base tree). Bash 3.2: checked by inspection only (no bash-3.2 binary locally); the code uses BASHPID with a sh PPID fallback, no associative arrays, mapfile or negative-index expansion.

## Regression Evidence

The issue brief (#40112) asks for no new tests by default: the flag ships off and the flag-off path is covered by the existing required suites (test-pulse-event-refill, test-dispatch-max-parallel, test-pulse-cycle-state-contract, test-pulse-wrapper-characterization, test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape, test-permission-block-breaker), all passing. Flag-on behaviour depends on live process liveness, PID reuse and wall-clock heartbeat ageing, which a hermetic repository test cannot reproduce faithfully. It was exercised manually through the real pulse-wrapper.sh --refill-only entry point against a live instance-lock holder (flag off: lock_busy lock=instance; flag on: dispatch lock acquired with owner_pid, instance lock untouched, no leaked lock), plus a throwaway harness covering overlap, stale reclaim, killed-subshell reclaim, nesting and the mode file. The platform-sensitive part (BASHPID with a sh PPID fallback for Bash 3.2) was checked by inspection, and with a forced-unset BASHPID the fallback resolved the real subshell PID rather than the top-level one. Runtime confirmation on macOS launchd comes from the brief's one-runner rollout comparison (#40109 report, 6 h before and after) before the default changes.

Resolves #40112

Recovery decisions recorded with wake=external_trigger never expired on time, so holds waiting on a site recovering or a date passing stayed status:blocked until someone replied or the repo policy changed. One runner had 25 such holds (median age 2.1 days, max 7.6), at least 13 with a written recheck time; three were already 9-14 h overdue. (2) _tbr_decision_active (terminal-blocker-recovery-release.sh) ends external_trigger suppression at recheck_after, or after BLOCKER_RECOVERY_EXTERNAL_TRIGGER_RECHECK (default 3 days) without one. human_decision keeps its positive-wake-only rule (GH#38692); other wakes keep the flat TTL; reply and policy-change wakes are unchanged. (3) The supervisor prompt (pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh) and reference/worker-integration-recovery.md + reference/recovery-policy.md tell the AI owner to set recheck_after and, on re-check, release or re-record. /decisions still lists these holds as parked. title: GH#40131: perf(recovery): batch supervisor queue issue reads
body:
## Summary

Resolves #40131 using the brief's measured-alternative acceptance path. The 3x target is **not established**.

- Batch up to four local circuit/remote-observation issue snapshots in the existing tier rotation. Bound selection and reads by the tier deadline; never advance cursors during prefetch.
- Reject all partial/error/null/truncated-label batches, disable further batching for that pass and retain individual REST-first fallback. Scratch data is private and scoped to the pass.
- Keep policy-gated and supervisor-only intakes in their original read order. Trusted complete comment reads, release guards and mechanical `rearm` remain unchanged.
- Reject newer/invalid timestamps before loading policy for an unchanged-decision fast path they cannot take. Eligible skips still require active decisions.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh`: bounded issue batch and snapshot fallback.
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-pending.sh`: tier-aware prefetch and per-pass scratch.
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: consume optional snapshot, expose the bounded stage, and order the timestamp predicate.
- `.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md`: operational behavior and measured limits.

## Measurements

Independent copies of the same real recovery store, identical initial cursors, 45-second `pending --count` budgets; no profiling writes targeted the live recovery store. Only aggregate counts are reported.

| Window | Entries | Baseline `entry_issue` | Final candidate `entry_issue` | Eligible `decided_unchanged` | Exit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Full queue | 79 | 8 | 9 (+12.5%) | 0 / 0 | 2 / 2 |
| Decided-only subset | 41 | 5 | 6 (+20%) | 1 / 1 | 2 / 2 |

Baseline/full elapsed 45.17s; candidate/full 44.73s. Baseline/decided 44.73s; candidate/decided 44.53s. The supervisor reserves part of the window for discovery. Local registration took approximately 0.8s, so network/policy/comment/revision work—not local queue validation—dominates. An intermediate batch-only candidate observed 9 full-store reads and 4 decided-window reads; timestamp-first validation improved the alternative. Small sequential windows are latency-sensitive and do not establish a general throughput guarantee or a 3x gain.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Exact head `bba68e37628a6c5ab40986fd2442faea66dfbebd`: copied-store production CLI runs above; 16 isolated runtime cases covering complete/partial/error/null/missing/truncated batches, invalid references, fallback and equal/older/newer/malformed/missing timestamps, invalid records, inactive decisions and rearm exclusion.
- Independent source review identified unbounded prefetch selection; deadline checks during selection and before cursor advancement repaired it. The full circuit suite exposed an intake read-order regression; excluding specialized intakes repaired it and the complete suite then passed.

## Verification

- `test-recovery-policy.sh`: 41 checks, zero failures.
- `test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`, `test-terminal-blocker-circuit-rearm.sh` and complete `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: final invocation exit 0, including the repaired unclassified-intake case and tier/cursor/rearm checks.

Its circuit failure was repaired and verified by the final direct suite. Final `affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base --max 4 --retries 0`: all four nearest suites passed, 242 transitive suites omitted by cap; no broad clean claim is made.

No release, permissions, trust policy or intake authority change.

title: t19330: perf(pulse): defer same-tier dispatch candidates after a no-selectable-model canary
body:
## Summary

When a worker canary exits 75/78 (no selectable model in the dispatch tier), Pulse now records a short-lived per-tier marker (`PULSE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE_TTL_SECONDS`, default 120s) under the headless-runtime state dir and probes the higher tiers with a local `select` (no model call). Later candidates whose resolved tier, and every tier above it, has a fresh marker are deferred in `dispatch_with_dedup` right after metadata validation. They return the existing GH#34428 defer rc (75): no dedup/eligibility gates, claim, comment, backoff, fast-fail or worktree. They keep their ranking and are recorded as `defer|…|reason=tier_unavailable`.

Why: from 2026-11-24 03:00–08:00Z, 721 of 725 ceremonies ran about 31s of GitHub-heavy gates and then failed at the canary because the Anthropic pool was exhausted.

Safety:
- The healthy path costs one stat, because the `thinking` marker must be fresh for any defer to happen.
- Other tiers are unaffected. A tier is only deferred when every tier that tier policy could raise it to is also proven unselectable.
- An explicit `model_override` is deferred only when the cached reasons line names that exact model as excluded. A selectable or unknown pin proceeds.
- Any canary result other than 75/78 clears the marker for its tier. Markers expire after the TTL.

Files:
- `pulse-dispatch-worker-model.sh`: extracted tier-only `_dlw_resolve_dispatch_tier`, shared with `_dlw_resolve_tier_and_model`.
- `pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`: marker record/clear/fresh, higher-tier probe, `_dlw_tier_unavailable_defers_candidate`, canary hooks.
- `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: early defer hook.
- `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `tier_unavailable` defer reason.
- `tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`: one focused regression case.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-model.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh

v4.13.19

What's Changed

  • fix(jsx): render an async component that returns null, a boolean, or a number in honojs/hono#5594
  • fix(jsx/dom): align useActionState with React 19 in honojs/hono#5635

  • fix(jsx/dom): keep keyed components in order when they update with a reorder in honojs/hono#5637
  • fix(bun): pass errors thrown in WebSocket handlers to onError in honojs/hono#5620
  • fix(proxy): drop Transfer-Encoding and Keep-Alive from the headers option in honojs/hono#5640
  • fix(method-override): drop the body when overriding to GET or HEAD in honojs/hono#5641
  • fix(jsx/dom): restore attributes and effects when Suspense children suspend again in honojs/hono#5642
  • fix(combine): continue the chain when a Condition returns true in every() in honojs/hono#5392
  • docs: fix JSDoc parameter types and missing annotations in middleware and helpers in honojs/hono#5409
  • fix(jsx/dom): keep a falsy Suspense fallback in honojs/hono#5644
  • fix(lambda-edge): omit body in a 204 result in honojs/hono#5643
  • fix(utils/types): stop JSONParsed at a recursive JSON type in honojs/hono#5645
  • feat(secure-headers): add an overwrite option in honojs/hono#5634
  • feat(jwt): add a typ option to verify the token header in honojs/hono#5639

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.13.18...v4.13.19

v4.13.18

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

validator() skips validation for requests whose Content-Type parameters are formatted differently

Affects: validator('json') and validator('form') in hono/validator. A Content-Type with whitespace before ;, a trailing ;, or an unusual parameter name was not recognized, so the validator saw an empty object while the handler could read all fields. This completes the fix for GHSA-4h7h-rv7c-7m2v. The validator now decides by the media type alone, as c.req.parseBody() does. GHSA-92p4-j3wq-jmqx

bodyLimit() keeps every transfer chunk of a request body in memory

Affects: bodyLimit() in hono/body-limit. A body sent in very small transfer chunks was retained as one object per chunk, so a request within the configured limit could exhaust memory. The body is now buffered in one array bounded by maxSize. GHSA-39q9-qp46-w8xg

mount() and app.mount() forward a wrong path when a custom getPath adds a prefix

Affects: mount() in hono/mount and app.mount() on 4.13.16 and 4.13.17. With a getPath that prepends a prefix such as the host name, one segment too many was removed from the forwarded path, so middleware scoped inside the mount prefix could be skipped. The prefix is removed from the routed path again. Paths that would change meaning when forwarded now get 400, and an optional regular expression parameter in a mount path throws. GHSA-h25j-2p75-qj33

serveStatic() serves a path that was decoded twice when allowPercentInPath is enabled

Affects: serveStatic() in hono/serve-static and the runtime adapters, only with allowPercentInPath: true. A malformed percent escape in the request path was decoded a second time, so a path that middleware registered on the encoded form did not see could still reach a static file. The file path must now be the same as the routed path, and otherwise the response is 404. GHSA-74fm-fwc7-3fwp

Users who rely on validator(), bodyLimit(), mount() with a custom getPath, or serveStatic() with allowPercentInPath are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.13.17...v4.13.18

Release notes

Sourced from anomalyco/opencode/github's releases.

v2.3.0

Highlights

  • Background Subagents by Default: Subagents now return immediately, continue in the background, and report back whenever they become idle. You can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently. (#63382)
  • Quieter Transcripts by Default: The TUI now summarizes each run of tool calls and thoughts into one collapsible activity row, so the answer is easier to follow. To see every step again, set Verbosity to medium or high in settings, or set session.verbosity in your TUI config; an existing setting is kept. (#63207)
  • Jump to an Earlier Prompt: In the desktop app, open Jump to message from the command palette or press Cmd+Alt+G (Ctrl+Alt+G on Windows and Linux) to search prompts across the current session and jump directly to one. (#63585)

Core

Improvements

  • Subagents now always run in the background, return their session ID immediately, and report results to their parent whenever they become idle. (#63382)
  • Added experimental support for MCP events, behind the mcp_events flag. (#63254, #63261, #63269)
  • Shell commands now survive server handoffs and keep their output when interrupted.
  • Added experimental support for moving a shell command to the background when its timeout expires, behind the shell_timeout_background flag. With the flag on, an explicit timeout on a background command stops it. (#63024, #63703)
  • Local Windows shell commands now run through the process daemon.
  • Added support for freeform tool input on compatible models.
  • Added LM Studio decision-model support.
  • Agents are now told when their session is a fork. Thanks @​hasta84. (#63235)
  • Tool output truncation now keeps the beginning of the output and preserves a usable preview if the full output cannot be saved.
  • Tail reads no longer load the entire file into memory.
  • Providers can present a client certificate for gateways that require mutual TLS. Set settings.tls with cert, key and an optional passphrase on the provider; values accept {file:} and {env:} like apiKey. (#61832)
  • When a subagent goes idle while its own background work is still running, its report to the parent now says it is still running, so the parent waits for the final report instead of treating the partial answer as done. (#63675)
  • Code Mode gets simpler structured results from file and skill tools: write and edit return their confirmation as a string, patch returns an empty result, and skill returns the skill's directory and content. (#63616, #63635, #63618, #63623)

Bug fixes

  • Fixed case-only file renames in patches on case-insensitive filesystems.
  • Fixed stale thinking being retained after Claude Agent prompts or tools change.
  • Fixed directly driven child sessions not resuming after a restart.
  • Fixed plugin replacement stopping when cleanup of an earlier plugin fails.
  • Fixed MCP OAuth refreshes and localhost redirects when a server rewrites 127.0.0.1.
  • Fixed saved API keys being omitted from local-model discovery.
  • Local model discovery (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) waits up to 15 seconds per request instead of 1, so remote or tunnelled endpoints list their models, and a slow endpoint no longer delays other endpoints or config reloads. (#63700)
  • In Code Mode, calling a namespace as if it were a tool now suggests up to three real tools under it. (#63697)
  • Fixed retryable provider streams losing completed work when interrupted.
  • Fixed GitHub Copilot requests using the wrong endpoint before models finish loading.
  • Fixed exhausted request rate limits being treated as terminal. Thanks @​Kyle-j-bush. (#59816)
  • Fixed LM Studio models with a null context length and accepted decision-type models. Thanks @​tomzhu1024. (#56214)

TUI

Improvements

  • Transcript verbosity now defaults to low, which summarizes each run of tools and thoughts into one activity row. A session.verbosity you already set is kept. (#63207)
  • Session IDs found in messages can now be opened directly.
  • Activity tabs are clickable and open the correct view.
  • Shell mode has its own prompt color under the new designs.

title: GH#40204: fix(pulse): recover orphaned self-device claims when exit-path CLAIM_RELEASED fails (GH#40204)
body:
## Summary

The stale sweep (_normalize_unassign_stale) skipped self-runner in-progress claims whenever any surviving process still named #N (for example a detached runtime subshell of the dead worker) or the recorded PID had been reused, so a worker whose exit-path CLAIM_RELEASED write failed stayed status:in-progress for hours. Those two skip reasons (now recorded in _NORMALIZE_STALE_SKIP_REASON) feed a bounded orphaned self-device claim check (_normalize_stale_try_orphan_recovery). It requires a local device id, no live process-group leader for session issue-N, no recent worker log, the newest DISPATCH_CLAIM/LEASE line and dispatch marker on this device and runner login, an expired lease, and a registered PID that is dead or no longer names the issue. Only then does it call dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned, which keeps its open-PR, branch-activity, issue-activity and interactive fences and writes the STALE_RECOVERED audit. Comment-reading checks are capped per sweep by AIDEVOPS_ORPHANED_SELF_CLAIM_CAP (default 5); live same-device workers are filtered locally first. The scan summary now logs orphan_checked/orphan_recovered.



## Files Changed

title: t19348: fix(bounded-operation): supervisor exits by natural drain to avoid Node 26 process.exit deadlock
body:
## Summary

The bounded-operation supervisor no longer ends with process.exit(), which can deadlock on Node 26 (nodejs/node#67596: the main thread joins a V8 background compile worker that is parked waiting for a main-thread GC). It sets process.exitCode, releases the IPC listeners and lets the event loop drain, with an unref'd 2 s process.exit fallback. The git-safety-gate fixture call now uses SIGKILL so its 10 s timeout can bound a wedged supervisor.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-supervisor.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs, TODO.md

title: t19349: fix(pulse): throughput report counts running and unlogged workers, adds ps census
body:
## Summary

Occupancy in pulse-throughput-report-helper.sh came only from spawn-to-exit pairs, and the only exit source was pulse.log `[lifecycle] worker_exited`. That parent-observer line covered about 47 of the 73 worker completions in headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl for 18:00-20:30. Still-running workers were dropped, and workers killed by the 17:28Z host reboot left no exit at all. Changes: (1) pair exits from both pulse.log and headless-runtime-metrics worker records, with a look-back that matches the six-hour spawn look-back; (2) add `slot_occupancy`, which also counts open intervals for unpaired spawns, each ending at the earliest of the next same-issue spawn, the longest paired runtime, the latest host boot (from a clock that keeps counting during sleep, so no subprocess) or now; (3) add `slot_occupancy_census` from Pulse's own per-round `Dispatch_capacity active_workers` ps count, plus the final admission target. Existing keys are kept and new keys are only added. The report is still read-only (no subprocesses, network or writes). Files: .agents/scripts/pulse_throughput_{report,events,logs,metrics}.py. Also marks t19345 complete (PR #40217).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse_throughput_events.py, .agents/scripts/pulse_throughput_logs.py, .agents/scripts/pulse_throughput_metrics.py, .agents/scripts/pulse_throughput_report.py, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19349-brief.md

## Decisions

Kept the interval estimate and also added the census rather than replacing it. The census is direct but only samples while rounds run, and it reads above the cap at times (max 29-33 on a 20 cap), so the two are reported side by side. Only the latest host boot can be detected without a subprocess, so earlier reboots fall back to the longest-paired-runtime bound. Paired-only means change slightly because runtime-metrics exits now pair too; that is a correction, not a regression.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Ran the report on the live logs. 17:45-20:30: before this change paired-only read 6.15 at 20:40 and 7.21 at 20:56. After: slot_occupancy 10.52 (2 open intervals, boot 17:28:07Z), census 10.55 (18 observations, coverage 0.67). 08:00-15:00: slot_occupancy 11.31, census 13.74. 18:00-now: 10.78 vs census 12.14. An intermediate version without the boot and runtime bounds read 31.5/20, which showed that reboot-killed spawns need the bound. `python3 -B -m py_compile` passes on all four modules. `--json` parses and the existing paired-only keys are unchanged.

Resolves #40220

title: t19351: fix(pulse): capacity halving counts only host/provider pressure failures
body:
## Summary

The worker capacity cap (`pulse-capacity.sh`) halved the worker target from 20 to 10 on task-outcome failures. Fewer concurrent workers cannot relieve those failures. After this change the cap counts only host and provider pressure failures. Guardrails and launch pacing keep their generic counts unchanged.

## Why

A point-in-time replay of the 2026-11-24 05:00–23:15Z `pulse.log` capacity observations (190 observations, 40 logged halvings) estimated 276 lost launch opportunities under the current rule and 78 with pressure-only failures. The most common halving inputs were:

- clean exits (`exit_code=0`) later failed by objective reconciliation
- claim and coordination outcomes (`worker_ownership_lost`, `merged_pr_reap`, …)
- worker blockers (`blocked`, `permission_required`)

None of these show host or provider saturation.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-terminal-health.py`: optional `--capacity-pressure` flag. In this mode, a failure is not counted when the exit was clean, the result is a task outcome (`TASK_OUTCOME_RESULTS`), or `failure_reason` is a coordination reason (`COORDINATION_REASONS`). Success counts and provider counters (rate limits, service interruptions, 5xx, progress) are unchanged. Without the flag, output is unchanged for the guardrail and pacing callers.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`: `_pulse_capacity_recent_health_counts` passes `--capacity-pressure`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`: new `test_capacity_counts_only_pressure_failures`. Of 10 failures (task outcomes plus premature exit, local error, watchdog stall, provider 5xx and 429), capacity counts 5 while guardrails and pacing keep 10. The existing reconciled-outcomes expectation drops the six unreconciled `permission_required` blockers from the capacity count (8 → 2).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`: clean
- `python3 -B -m py_compile .agents/scripts/worker-terminal-health.py`: clean
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`: 30 run, 0 failed
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`: 170 run, 0 failed
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`: 37 run, 0 failed

Runtime check after deploy:

```bash
rg -n 'worker_terminal_failures=' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -20
```

Expect fewer capacity halvings in windows where failures are task outcomes. Provider 429 and 5xx signals still halve the target.

Resolves #40226

title: t19352: fix(pulse): stale-assignment sweep discovers dead-worker claims with one search every normalize run
body:
## Summary

The stale-assignment sweep is the only backstop that returns a dead worker's `status:in-progress`/`status:queued` claim to the queue. It listed every pulse repo inside a normalize stage budget shared with four other listing passes, so it almost never finished. This PR finds the runner's stale active claims with **one** `search/issues` call on every normalize run. Each candidate is re-read live, then goes through the unchanged skip gate and audited reset. The pending checkpoint-lease and deferred claim-release drains also run on every run instead of waiting for that pass's turn.

## Why

Measured on one macOS runner with 101 pulse repos, from `pulse-stage-timings.log` and `pulse.log` since 2026-11-22:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| `normalize_active_issue_assignments` runs | 43 |
| Runs killed by the stage watchdog | 42 |
| `Stale assignment scan:` summary lines in the current `pulse.log` | 0 |
| One fleet-wide `search/issues` call for this runner's stale active claims | about 1 s |

In a private managed repo, two claims with dead worker PIDs stayed `status:in-progress` for 1.8 h and 2.5 h. The earlier partial fixes (GH#37362, GH#37565, GH#37568) kept discovery O(repos). The GH#40204 orphan recovery (PR #40207) runs inside the same starved sweep. Brief: #40231.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
  - `_normalize_stale_process_candidate`: the per-candidate gate, orphan hook, `CLAIM_RELEASED` audit and reset, extracted unchanged so both passes share one path.
  - `_normalize_unassign_stale_search`:
    - Sends one search: `is:issue is:open assignee:<runner> label:"status:in-progress","status:queued" updated:<cutoff>`, oldest first, `per_page=100`.
    - Keeps only non-local `repos.json` repos that pass `repo_allows_pulse_write_actions`.
    - Skips live same-device session leaders before any API read.
    - Re-reads every other candidate live, because search can lag, and drops closed, relabelled, reassigned or freshly updated issues.
    - Checks at most `AIDEVOPS_STALE_SEARCH_MAX_CANDIDATES` candidates (default 20), oldest first.
    - Returns 1 when the search fails, `incomplete_results` is not `false`, or the match count exceeds one page, so the per-repo pass still runs.
    - Always logs `Stale assignment scan (search): …`.
  - `_normalize_claim_recovery_every_run`: search sweep, then both drains, each with substage timing.
  - `_normalize_stale_per_repo_backstop_due`: decides when the per-repo pass still runs.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `normalize_active_issue_assignments`
  - Calls the every-run recovery after the dead-stamp reap.
  - Skips the per-repo `unassign_stale` pass when search coverage was complete and the pass started within `AIDEVOPS_STALE_PER_REPO_BACKSTOP_S` (default 6 h). The pass is kept as a backstop because search can silently omit repos the token cannot search, such as an org whose SSO has not authorised it. A skipped pass is not stamped, so it sorts first when due.
  - Moves the per-pass notes into the function header so the body stays under the 100-line function gate.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-rotation.sh`: `_normalize_pass_started_within`, a reader for the existing pass-start stamps.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-search.sh` (new, 12 cases): reset through the real gate with exactly one search, query shape, session-leader skip with no issue read, live recheck, repo filtering, cap ordering, search failure, incomplete results, page limit, and coordinator ordering, fallback and backstop.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh`: adds the search sweep to the safety-function contracts (ignores maintenance/Pulse state, keeps the write-authority guard).

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on all changed shell files: clean. Pre-commit ratchets pass. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check` reports no new violations for function-complexity, nesting-depth or bash32-compat.
- `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-search.sh` 12/12, `test-issue-reconcile.sh` 20/20, `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-orphaned-self-claim.sh` 11/11, `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr.sh` 14/14, `test-reassign-self-normalization.sh` 11/11, `test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh` pass, `test-reconcile-budget-isolation.sh` 8/8, `test-reconcile-single-pass-cursor.sh` 41/41, `test-dispatch-dedup-multi-operator.sh` 10/10, `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` pass, `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` 54/54, `test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py` 46/46.
- Read-only live discovery check (search, row filter, live recheck and session-leader probe only; no gate, comment or label write) against the real runner:
  - The search returned 8 matches with `incomplete_results=false`. Every row still rechecked as a stale claim.
  - 6 had a live same-device session leader and would be skipped with no further API call.
  - The 2 dead-PID claims from the evidence above would reach the gate.
  - The test also caught a defect fixed before this PR: jq's `//` treats `false` as missing, so `.incomplete_results // true` marked every complete search as incomplete.

Runtime check after deploy:

```bash
rg -c 'Stale assignment scan \(search\):' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
rg 'Stale assignment (scan \(search\)|reset):' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -20
```

Expect a search summary on every normalize run. Expect dead-PID active claims released within one or two runs (about 25–50 min) instead of hours.

Resolves #40231
For #40108

title: t19356: feat(workers): keep prompt cache warm during long tool calls; require repeated failure before Opus escalation
body:
## Summary

One private data-pipeline worker fleet accounted for about 85% of local Anthropic spend over 3 days. This PR fixes two systemic wastes there without lowering throughput.

### 1. Cache rebuilds after long tool calls (root cause of the "re-read context" waste)

The Anthropic prompt cache expires 5 minutes after its last read. These workers often wait in tool calls longer than that:

- a repository-owned shared lock wrapper: median 354s over 541 calls
- `pnpm install`: median 369s over 123 calls

The next request then re-writes the whole context at 1.25x. In the local session DB, 130.9M cache-write tokens followed 5–60 minute gaps. That is **29.9% of all that fleet's cache writes**.

- New `cache-keepalive.mjs`. While a tool call is still running, it re-sends the session's last agent request with `max_tokens: 1` and `stream: false`. It does this every 4 minutes, at most 5 times per gap. The refresh goes through the same body transforms and headers as the real request, with a bounded 60s timeout. It fails open.
- `provider-auth.mjs` records completed 2xx streamed requests that carry tools. Tool hooks in `index.mjs` track running tools per session.
- Requests with a fixed `thinking.budget_tokens` are skipped, because `max_tokens` must exceed the budget. Adaptive thinking is fine.
- Opt out with `AIDEVOPS_CACHE_KEEPALIVE=0`.
- **Live verification:** real OAuth seat, Sonnet 5.5, with redistribution and CCH transforms applied.
  - The agent request wrote 37,306 cache tokens.
  - The keep-alive replay read 37,306 cached tokens, wrote 0, and returned 1 output token.
- A blanket 1-hour TTL was simulated at +5.9% net cost and rejected. This keep-alive only spends during real tool waits.

### 2. Opus escalation after a single non-capability failure

All recent automatic `tier:standard → tier:thinking` escalations in that repo fired at `failures=1` with crash type `overwhelmed`. The reasons were only ever two:

- `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`: the PR exists and only the handoff check failed.
- `watchdog_stall_killed`.

Neither shows that Sonnet cannot do the task. About 131 sessions ran on Opus at roughly 5x the per-session cost. Consolidated successors then copy the `tier:thinking` label from their parent.

Changes:

- `escalate_issue_tier`: escalation **into** `thinking` now needs `ESCALATION_THINKING_MIN_FAILURES` cumulative failures (default 2). `simple → standard` still escalates on one `overwhelmed` failure.
- PR handoff failures never escalate into `thinking`. These are `worker_post_pr_handoff_*`, `worker_closed_unmerged_pr` and `worker_ready_missing_*`, the same family `_fast_fail_reason_wants_enrichment` already skips.
- The threshold check uses `-ge` instead of `-eq`. The count is cumulative, so an issue that already moved `simple → standard` can still reach the higher threshold. Tier labels keep this idempotent. The body-quality diagnostic posts once, at the threshold.
- The consolidation prompt (`pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`) copies a parent's `tier:*` only when a maintainer set it. A cascade-escalated parent passes on its pre-escalation tier.
- The Opus path remains for repeated real failures, as requested.

### Guidance

`.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md` now covers:

- measuring cache-break gaps start-to-start, because `llm_requests.timestamp` is the finish time and includes tool time;
- the keep-alive behaviour and opt-out;
- preferring fail-fast lock checks over long blocking waits in repository workflows.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-tier-routing.sh`: 15/15. New cases cover:
  - one failure keeps standard on standard;
  - repeated failure escalates;
  - PR handoff failures are exempt.
- `shellcheck` on changed shell files: clean.
- `node --test tests/test-cache-keepalive.mjs tests/test-oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs tests/test-provider-auth-cch.mjs`: 18/18 pass. The rotation probe's isolation allowlist now includes the timer-only `cache-keepalive.mjs`.
- Qlty new-file findings (`return-statements`, `function-complexity`, `boolean-logic`) were fixed in code. The scheduler is now a small class with one-purpose methods, and body eligibility is a check list. Biome is clean.
- Full plugin suite: two load-sensitive failures, in `test-registered-value-redaction.mjs` and `test-runtime-events.mjs`. Both pass when run alone, and neither touches the changed code.
- Escalation-related shell suites: all pass. These cover fast-fail age-out, orphan lock, failure classification, tier-label ratchet, self-hosting detector and no-work reclassification.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Lock hold time in the affected repo is tracked in that repo's own issues.
- pnpm workspace worktrees fall through to a full install. Provisioning restores one `node_modules` under a 64 MiB cap, and workspace members without their own lockfile are skipped. Tracked in #40257.
- `v2-provider-auth.mjs` does not yet record keep-alive requests. OpenCode v1 is the active path. Tracked in #40264.

Resolves #40251

body:
## Summary

Adds mailbox-side keep-and-copy filters to purelymail-helper.sh over ManageSieve. New purelymail_sieve.py is a stdlib ManageSieve client (STARTTLS with hostname verification, AUTHENTICATE PLAIN, LISTSCRIPTS/GETSCRIPT/CHECKSCRIPT/PUTSCRIPT/SETACTIVE/RENAMESCRIPT/DELETESCRIPT); it reads the password from the injected env var named in argv, never the value. copy-to writes the Roundcube-format script named 'roundcube', refuses foreign or edited scripts, no-ops when the same filter is active, and verifies by read-back + active check. copy-to-remove needs --yes, refuses webmail-edited scripts, and deletes only the exact contents it checked (rename aside, re-read, delete or restore). Docs: services/email/purelymail.md 'Keep and copy (Sieve filter)'.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/purelymail-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/purelymail_sieve.py, .agents/services/email/purelymail.md

## Decisions

1) Separate purelymail_sieve.py instead of the review's inline python heredoc: testable on its own and keeps the shell helper small. 2) Live probe found the real quirk differs from the issue text: Purelymail (Apache James ManageSieve, VERSION 1.0) re-sends capabilities in PLAINTEXT after STARTTLS OK, before the handshake, and none over TLS. The client drains and discards that unauthenticated listing, then synchronises over TLS with `NOOP "aidevops-sync"`, reading up to the first data-less reply (or NO). That consumes an RFC capability listing however late it arrives, with no timing assumption (CodeRabbit finding). 3) copy-to-remove passes the checked script to the client, which runs RENAMESCRIPT to a parked name, compares, and deletes only on match; otherwise it renames back, or keeps the parked copy if webmail recreated the name meanwhile (CodeRabbit finding). A retry after an interrupted removal finds `roundcube.aidevops-remove`, applies the same check and `--yes` gate, and finishes the removal; a parked foreign script exits 1 (CodeRabbit finding). 4) PURELYMAIL_SIEVE_HOST/PORT env overrides exist for local test servers only.

## Implementation

The config hook registers runtime rules independently of signed grants. The read-target classifier follows the broker's existing one-shot allowance path. Physical scratch roots are anchored to resolved home plus the literal managed suffix; symlink relocation cannot redefine the boundary. Changed files and verification follow the corrected canonical issue Files Scope.

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs`

Reference pattern: existing managed-directory registration and broker one-shot allowance path. Independent read-only security review found two defects; both were fixed and re-reviewed with no remaining actionable defects.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Exact head 05094efd45 on macOS, OpenCode 1.19.6, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5: real headless opencode run sessions with AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true, WORKER_WORKTREE_PATH and an inert worker issue number set, no repo slug, and the broker blocker log and permission-request capture redirected to a scratch directory. Each run used an isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME that mirrors the global OpenCode config with only the plugin entry swapped (an OPENCODE_CONFIG override loads both plugin copies, so it was not used), plus an isolated XDG_DATA_HOME with a copied auth file. The same probes ran against the deployed v3.39.282 plugin as a baseline; every rejected probe ran in its own fresh session. opencode debug config: the head adds /dev/null, /dev/stdin, /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr, /dev/fd/* and the absolute managed tmp root to the global and Build+ external_directory rules; the baseline has none of them, and neither has a /proc rule. title: t19359: fix(disk-capacity): count APFS purgeable capacity toward the worktree percentage floor (GH#40266)
body:
## Summary

On macOS the disk gate now lets APFS important-usage capacity (df headroom plus purgeable space such as Time Machine local snapshots, which macOS reclaims on demand) satisfy the capped 5% percentage floor. The probe is read-only JXA (NSURLVolumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey, path passed as argv, bounded runner) and runs only when raw df is below the floor. The absolute 5 GiB minimum and quota checks stay on raw df so purge latency cannot reach ENOSPC. AIDEVOPS_DISK_COUNT_PURGEABLE=0 restores the raw-only policy. Pulse logs the first purgeable admission per process. The reclaim-hint timeout selection now shares the new bounded-runner helper.



## Files Changed

## Decisions

GH#38026 kept backup retention with the owner; this keeps that boundary (aidevops never thins snapshots) and uses the capacity Apple designates for user-initiated writes instead of raw df, so the gate no longer waits on a human to thin backups. Raw df still governs the absolute floor and cleanup-headroom trigger, so cleanup keeps running in pressure mode.

title: t19364: perf(pulse): give split-lock refill dispatch-lock holder the elastic dispatch lease
body:
## Summary

Under PULSE_DISPATCH_LOCK_SPLIT=1, a worker-exit refill-only run holds the dispatch lock (not the instance lock) for its whole drain, and the cycle's own dispatch stages skip while it does (104 'dispatch lock held' skips, 2026-11-24/25). Only the instance-lock owner had the elastic dispatch lease, so most dispatch ran on a fixed per-pass clock: 54 round endings were candidate-admission-reserve stops versus 10 'no available worker slots', each followed by a fresh 80-205s census; pass boundaries matched the largest idle gaps (05:56Z 338s, 06:19Z 602s). New _pulse_dispatch_lock_lease_active in pulse-watchdog.sh gives the lease to a PULSE_REFILL_ONLY=1 process that does not own the instance lock, still owns the dispatch lock (pulse_dispatch_lock_still_owned) and has a dispatch-lock heartbeat no older than PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S. Candidate admission refreshes that heartbeat and contenders reclaim a stale holder at the same ceiling, so a hung holder stays bounded; round top-ups, PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_MAX_PASSES, stop flag and between-pass bundle/transition checks are unchanged. Default off: without the split flag a refill-only run never owns the dispatch lock.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19364-brief.md

title: GH#40309: fix: keep bounded-operation supervisor alive after an exited command and make load-flaky plugin tests deterministic (GH#40309)
body:
## Summary

Root cause: on a loaded host the supervisor's grace-timer escalation could fire after the drain had already observed the command's exit, SIGKILLing the supervisor's own group and turning a clean exit into an unknown/incomplete result. The terminator now records drained state, skips escalation once drained, and for an already-exited command kills only the other group members (keeping a bounded group-SIGKILL backstop). Command start identity is captured on a later track tick when the spawn-time ps snapshot is missed, and ps snapshots retry once with a longer timeout on ETIMEDOUT. Test fixes: gate-file instead of wall-clock bound for start; GH#33514 test uses progress markers and holds back only the operation budget timer; unique operation IDs in test-git-safety-gate (concurrent runs adopted each other's supervisors); oauth lock test asserts ordering via a stdin-gated Python holder instead of elapsed time; redaction test lists only the probe pid instead of the whole host ps table; termination-case budget uses SUCCESS_BUDGET_MS.

title: t19362: feat(plugin): retry sessions stopped by provider Overloaded errors after 60 s (GH#40283)
body:
## Summary

OpenCode retries an overloaded provider inside a turn for about a minute, then stops the session with an error such as Anthropic HTTP 529 'Overloaded', and nothing resumes it. New provider-overload-retry.mjs (state machine), provider-overload-client.mjs (SDK lookups and prompting) and provider-overload-policy.mjs (classification, settings, request identity) watch session.error and session.idle. After a terminal overload on a root interactive session they wait 60 s, re-check that the session is idle and the user has not sent anything, then send one synthetic continuation with the same agent, model and variant, telling the model not to repeat completed side effects. A user message, a completed reply or a busy session cancels the pending retry; unknown status or identity fails closed. Child sessions, headless runs and non-overload errors (auth, request, context length, cancellation) are never retried. Episodes stop after 5 retries without a completed reply and show a toast. Settings: AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY=0 disables; AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS (default 60, max 3600); AIDEVOPS_OVERLOAD_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5, max 50). session-turn-outcomes.mjs suppresses its 'Nothing was retried' toast for overloads that will be retried. Documented in reference/safety-stop-recovery.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-overload-client.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-overload-policy.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-overload-retry.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-turn-outcomes.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-overload-retry.mjs, .agents/reference/safety-stop-recovery.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime, exact head: real opencode serve (OpenCode 1.19.6) loading this worktree's plugin, with a fake Anthropic-compatible provider that streams the real overloaded_error event (delay 4 s, max 3 for the check). Scenario A: OpenCode's own retries ended in session.error APIError 'Overloaded' at 72.8 s; the plugin showed the 'Provider overloaded' toast, sent '[synthetic] AIDEVOPS PROVIDER OVERLOAD RETRY (1/3)' at 77.1 s with agent build and model fakeanthropic/fake-model, and the session answered RECOVERED. Scenario B: the user sent a message 1 s after the terminal error; 0 retry prompts were sent and the user's turn answered normally. Focused tests: node --test tests/test-provider-overload-retry.mjs and the provider diagnostics/turn-outcome suites pass, including fail-closed status/identity, 100-message lookback and takeover during root lookup. An independent review found no P0/P1 defects; its three P2 findings are fixed in this head.; flaky plugin tests (failed in the full suite, passed on serialized rerun; not blocking): npm run test (.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops): explicit audited adoption enables a previous session worktree without taking a live owner | restoration disposal cannot become success after exit-zero TERM cleanup | JavaScript waits for the live Python owner of the shared lock
