title: t19368: perf(sandbox): share one macOS process-table read across concurrent worker wait loops
body:
## Summary

On macOS, every sandboxed worker's wait loop read the full host process table (`ps -axo pid=,ppid=,pgid=,stat=,lstart=`) every 0.5 s to snapshot its descendants. A read costs ~45 ms CPU per ~1,500 processes, so the watchers' cost scaled as workers x host processes: about 1.3 cores for 16 workers on a runner already at load 208-272 with 0% idle.

- `_sandbox_shared_ps_table`: one host-wide table (`$SANDBOX_DIR/ps-table`, `#ts=` header from `EPOCHREALTIME`) reused while younger than the TTL (default 500 ms = one poll interval, so sampling density is unchanged).
- Refresh lock: the noclobber-created staging file `ps-table.next` is the lock, and the rename that publishes it releases it. A loop that finds a refresh in progress reuses a table up to four TTLs old instead of duplicating the read. A dead writer's staging file is reclaimed after 2 s.
- `_sandbox_descendant_rows`: indexes rows by parent and splits/joins columns only for descendants. Output is byte-identical to the old awk.
- Safety: the table is trusted only if this user owns the dir and file and neither is a symlink. Otherwise, or with Bash lacking `EPOCHREALTIME`, or `AIDEVOPS_SANDBOX_PS_TABLE_TTL_MS=0`, reads stay direct. The cleanup-time final snapshot always bypasses the cache, and per-PID identity revalidation before any signal is unchanged.
- Linux `/proc` walk unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19368-brief.md

## Decisions

- TTL defaults to the poll interval so no loop samples less often than before; the 4xTTL stale-reuse bound applies only while another loop is mid-refresh.
- The awk uses `-v pid_col=1 -v ppid_col=2` field variables: the positional-parameter ratchet strips single-quoted segments per line only, so field refs inside multi-line awk programs are flagged. The validator gap is filed separately as GH#40335.
- `test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh` "SIGKILL child exits helper promptly" (3 s threshold) failed once at load 258, then passed 3/3 on this branch and 3/3 on main at load ~205. The path it times (poll detection plus fresh final snapshot) is not changed here.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified on the 16-core macOS runner that motivated the change (load 208-272, 0% idle):

- Existing suites, all green from the worktree: test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh (macOS descendant cleanup incl. escaped groups), test-sandbox-timeout-budget.sh (4/4), test-sandbox-command-policy.sh (61/61), test-sandbox-passthrough-otel.sh (7/7), test-sandbox-sensitive-output-guard.sh (7/7), test-agent-sandbox-helper.sh (32/32), test-output-sandbox-helper.sh (49/49).
- End-to-end `sandbox-exec-helper.sh run --timeout 20 sleep 2`: exit 0; `ps-table` refreshed during the run; no `ps-table.next` left behind.
- Output equivalence: the old and new descendant awk produce byte-identical rows (shasum) from one live table read for roots 1 (1,551 descendants = whole host), three live sandbox wrappers (10, 10, 14 rows), an interactive opencode (1) and a missing PID (0).
- Behaviour checks (16/16): table published with `#ts=` header; shared rows == fresh rows; reuse within TTL; refresh after TTL; future stamp treated as stale; held lock reuses a table within four TTLs and leaves the lock; held lock + too-stale table falls back to a direct read; dead writer's staging file older than 2 s reclaimed; noclobber not leaked; TTL=0 disables; symlinked table refused; missing dir falls back with identical rows; no temp leftovers.
- Cost: one poll's descendant snapshot drops from ~52 ms CPU (fresh full-table ps + awk) to ~10 ms when the shared table is fresh. A 16-poller concurrent benchmark (random phases, ps invocations counted through a PATH shim) measured 70.8-72.2 ms CPU/poll with direct reads (1 ps per poll) versus 23.1-32.3 ms/poll shared (full ps on 8-23% of polls). Before the refresh lock, the herd refreshed on ~50% of polls.
- Baseline motivating measurement: live wrappers' lifetime self+reaped-child CPU was 0.08-0.09 cores each (16 wrappers, ~1.3 cores).; macOS: native platform detection, model replay sandbox and PATH portability checks passed at 3c43cdb7da329f5acaf66a515f90527b65648194.

## Regression Evidence

No repository test is added. A deterministic regression for cross-process table sharing needs concurrent wait loops, a counting `ps` PATH shim and wall-clock TTL control. That is new test infrastructure, which repository policy (reference/ci-gate-policy.md) requires maintainer approval for. The changed descendant-snapshot path is already exercised end to end on macOS by the existing sandbox suites listed under Testing, and the macOS local suite passed on this head. Manual evidence: old and new descendant extraction are byte-identical for six live roots; 16/16 scripted cache behaviour checks (TTL reuse/refresh, refresh lock, stale-lock reclaim, symlink refusal, TTL=0 opt-out, fallback); a 16-poller benchmark cut CPU from 70.8-72.2 to 23.1-32.3 ms per poll.

Resolves #40332

title: t19371: perf(full-loop): check platform regression evidence before the native macOS suites in commit-and-pr
body:
## Summary

`commit-and-pr` ran the Platform Fix Regression Evidence gate (GH#39136) only after `macos_checks_evidence`, so a missing `--regression-evidence` rationale failed after the full native macOS run. t19368 / PR #40341 lost ~31 minutes this way on a loaded runner, then had to repeat the suites. The gate's verdict cannot depend on those suites: it reads the title, the changed paths and body prose outside Files Changed/Testing/Regression Evidence headings, and the suites only append Runtime Testing evidence.

- `_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata` resolves the PR title (unchanged `_compose_pr_title` / `_validate_explicit_pr_title` block) before the macOS suites, then calls `_commit_and_pr_platform_evidence_preflight`.
- The preflight renders the gate-visible prose in the final body's order and headings (Summary, Decisions, Regression Evidence, then `Resolves #N`, the longest closing line the final body can place after Regression Evidence) and runs the existing `_commit_and_pr_platform_evidence_gate`. A preflight refusal implies a final refusal; the final gate after the body is built stays authoritative.
- `_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata` stays at 100 lines (function-length gate). The two test harnesses that eval it also load the new helper.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19371-brief.md

## Decisions

- The preview body mirrors the final layout, including the closing line after Regression Evidence, instead of a minimal rationale-only check. The gate today counts that closing line as rationale text (filed separately), so a stricter preview could refuse a body CI accepts.
- No new test: the changed path is covered by the existing harnesses (updated to load the helper) plus the parity run above.

title: t19374: perf(profile): bound profile README SQLite reads so the hourly routine cannot pin the llm-requests WAL
body:
## Summary

The hourly profile README routine (r908, launchd Background) held one read transaction on llm-requests.db for 7h06m on a saturated host, using 16 s of CPU, which pinned the WAL at 11.3 GB. After the reader was terminated, the WAL checkpointed back to 0.7 MB. The queries are cheap at normal priority (obs DB 2-4 s warm; full `generate` 224 s including the OpenCode all-time scan), so this caps the starved case and does not rewrite the queries. Every profile SQLite read now goes through `_profile_sqlite_read`: `sqlite3 -readonly` with a 5 s busy timeout, under `timeout_sec ${PROFILE_README_SQLITE_TIMEOUT_S:-300}`, with one stderr warning on timeout. The fail-soft fallback contract is unchanged. `profile-readme-helper.sh` now sources `shared-constants.sh`: it never did before, so `timeout_sec` was unavailable to the routine. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN disproved the original CTE-materialization hypothesis (identical plans, no MATERIALIZE on SQLite 3.51), so that rewrite was dropped. Also marks t19371 done in TODO.md (PR #40344 merged).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19374-brief.md

title: t19376: perf(headless): disable OpenCode fff file index for headless workers so worktree churn stops costing up to a core per worker
body:
## Summary

Headless worker launches now export OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1 inside the launch subshell (new _invoke_opencode_disable_fff beside the GH#38491 snapshot switch in .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh). OpenCode 1.19.6 then uses its ripgrep FileSystem/Search backend instead of the native fff index. On a 16-core runner, 3 of 6 live workers sat at 0.66-0.90 lifetime CPU share; a 3 s sample of the hottest showed fff's background watcher re-running libgit2 status (git_status_for_paths -> git_diff_index_to_workdir -> git_pathspec__match -> dowild/tolower) over a 49,870-entry index during installs and builds. fff grep also stops after timeBudgetMs 1500, which can silently truncate worker results on a saturated host; the ripgrep backend runs glob and grep live on every call. A caller-set OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF wins; AIDEVOPS_WORKER_OPENCODE_FFF=1 opts out. Interactive sessions are unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19376-brief.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime: launched a real worker from this branch via headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role worker --tier simple --standalone-prompt (model openai/gpt-6-luna, sandboxed, isolated DB). ps eww on the live opencode run child showed OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1 beside OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={"snapshot":false}; a production worker on the deployed release showed only the snapshot config. title: t19386: fix(terminal-blocker): map a login input owner through verified repo permission
body:
## Summary

Workers that end with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=input_required` sometimes name a GitHub login as `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER` instead of a role. That was classified `unknown`, so the question was dropped and the issue was redispatched to ask it again. The capture now treats one login-shaped owner as a candidate only. It maps the login through the repository's collaborator-permission API (`role_name`, falling back to `permission`): `admin` gives `input_required:admin`, `maintain`/`write` give `input_required:maintainer`, and anything else stays `unknown` with the question cleared. The login is validated in both Python and Bash, is never published, and only chooses who is asked. Releasing the hold still needs OWNER/MEMBER evidence. Malformed role words (for example `Admin ` with trailing whitespace) are not treated as logins.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md, .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t19386-brief.md

The scheduled OpenCode DB archive stopped making progress: 89 of 91 per-DB runs in one archive cycle hit the 60 s deadline. Two causes, both fixed here. (1) get_active_worker_sessions forked a stat subshell per pulse log (720+ logs over the 48 h retention, ~1,450 forks per call); under launchd background QoS that scan alone outlasted the per-DB budget. It is now one find -mmin -61 scan with batched grep and sort -u (BSD find rounds age up to whole minutes, so -61 keeps every log the old 3600 s check kept). (2) The deadline stop() handler only caught ProcessLookupError, but Darwin killpg() returns EPERM when every group member has exited but is not yet reaped; the uncaught PermissionError turned budget deferrals (rc=2, resume next cycle) into rc=1 failures with a traceback (75 tracebacks in the live archive log).



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh

## Decisions

Kept scope to the production paths. Did not make the deadline tests load-tolerant or isolate them from the host pulse-log directory in this PR; that is test hygiene, tracked separately.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Live pulse-log directory: old and new get_active_worker_sessions produce identical output (143 lines, same SHA-256 prefix); old scan 8.53-10.89 s, new 0.71 s. Small-DB dry run under taskpolicy -b nice -n 10: >400 s before, 19.03 s after. shellcheck clean. test-opencode-db-archive.sh at load average 111 on 16 cores: main aborts at test 2 (first archive exceeds its 30 s budget in the pulse-log scan, then the EPERM traceback gives rc=1); this branch runs the whole suite, 82 passed and 7 failed, and the traceback is gone (deadline path now returns rc=2). The 7 failures are the 10 s-budget commit_gap and in-flight-marker cases: under that load a 164 KB fixture spends 2-5 s in event expiry, so the copy never commits before the deadline and the later checks fail as a result. Pre-existing load sensitivity, not changed by this PR.

## Regression Evidence

No new test is added because the Darwin EPERM depends on kernel reap timing: killpg() returns EPERM only when every process in the group has exited and none has been reaped yet. That cannot be reproduced deterministically in a unit test. The existing deadline cases in .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh (SQLite candidate/commit_gap and per-DB preflight/batch deadlines) already drive stop() through killpg on macOS. Before this change they produced the PermissionError traceback and rc=1 (logged run on main, same host). After it they return the expected rc=2 deferral with no traceback. The pulse-log scan change is covered by the identical-output comparison against the live log directory recorded in Runtime Testing.

Resolves #40443

title: GH#40451: OAuth MCP login reaches aidevops-launched OpenCode sessions
body:
## Summary

(1) mcp-activation-tool recognises needs_auth / needs_client_registration and fails on the first poll (no 30s wait, no bounded reset) with the login command for this process's credential store, built only from the registry name and XDG_DATA_HOME (shell-quoted), never from status detail. (2) opencode-launcher-helper seeds mcp-auth.json for interactive TUI, desktop and server stores only when the session store has none yet: a copy of the global store (exactly one JSON object), created mode 600 with a no-clobber hard link, best-effort, contents never printed. An existing session store is never replaced. Conversation and remote/Buzz stores are untouched. (3) mcp-diagnose.sh uses the plugin registry type for registry-only servers and, for alwaysOverwrite entries, only for the OpenCode runtime's config, so sentry reports [remote] plus status and login commands for the same shell-escaped store instead of npm install. Other runtimes keep their configured type. (4) services/monitoring/sentry.md documents the remote OAuth flow and drops the SENTRY_YOURNAME token setup. The launcher test now unsets XDG_DATA_HOME so fixtures never read the running session's real credential store.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs, .agents/scripts/mcp-diagnose.sh, .agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh, .agents/services/monitoring/sentry.md

## Decisions

Seeding never replaces an existing session store. OAuth refresh rotates tokens there, and OpenCode takes no writer lock, so any read-then-replace merge could drop a rotated refresh token (review thread r4703715692). Existing stores use the store-scoped login command printed by `aidevops_mcp connect` and mcp-diagnose.sh. Seeding is limited to the user's interactive/desktop/server stores; conversation (team interface) and remote-hosted stores never receive the user's MCP OAuth tokens. needs_client_registration gets a distinct message since a plain re-login may not fix it.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime: started a real `opencode serve` (OpenCode 1.19.6) on a fresh isolated XDG_DATA_HOME and drove the changed activation tool against it over HTTP; real status for unauthenticated sentry is needs_auth, and connect returned in 1068 ms: 'MCP sentry needs an OAuth login for this session's credential store (status needs_auth). Run in a terminal, then connect again: XDG_DATA_HOME='<tmp store>' opencode mcp auth sentry'. Real `mcp-diagnose.sh sentry` on this host (user config holds a legacy disabled local sentry entry) now prints [remote] type remote and the session-store login command; `mcp-diagnose.sh netbird` keeps the local path. Launcher: test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh passes (real helper, fake opencode), including new seed cases: a missing session store receives the global object with mode 600 and no token text in output; an existing session store is left unchanged; a global file holding two JSON values creates no store. test-mcp-activation.mjs passes (new case: both auth statuses fail on the first poll, no reset, no status detail leaked). shellcheck and markdownlint clean. Not exercised: the browser OAuth approval itself (OpenCode-owned).

Resolves #40451

## Testing

`file-split-verify.py --base origin/main --head HEAD`: `removed=2510 added=2618 removed-only=26 review=34 result=FAIL`. All 26 removed-only lines are not logic changes. The three cases:

title: t19417: fix(tests): surface and fix Linux-only red health suites (GH#40529)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the remaining Linux-runner-only red suites in Shell Suite Main Health.

- `test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` (exit 2 on hosted runners): `worker-registry retire-enrolled-only` takes a real, fail-closed `/proc` census. A same-UID non-dumpable task makes `/proc/<pid>/cwd` unreadable, and hosted runners have such tasks. Production then correctly refuses with `.process_observation = {stage:"cwd", cause:"inspection-not-enabled"}`. The suite sent that JSON to `/dev/null`, so `set -e` exited 2 and printed nothing. The suite now captures the refusal. It skips that one assertion only when census-unavailability evidence is present and the tree was kept. Any other refusal fails and prints the JSON. An `ERR` trap also names the line of any unexpected `set -e` exit.
- `affected-tests-helper.sh --log-dir`: suite logs kept only the last 80 lines, so the `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` FAIL line (1/230) was cut from the artifact. The log now also keeps up to 40 earlier `FAIL`/error lines before the tail.

Census root cause credit: the GH#40410 session (commit `5470f33b1d`), folded in here.

## Verification

- `docker run ubuntu:24.04` as non-root `runner` with a same-UID `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)` process: previously rc=2. Now rc=0 with `SKIP registry retirement: host process census unavailable (cwd/inspection-not-enabled); refusal kept the tree`.
- macOS: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` passes, and the real retirement path still runs (`PASS registry retirement archives ...`).
- `shellcheck` is clean on both changed scripts.
- Branch dispatch of `shell-suite-main-health.yml`: see the comment below for the run result and the pr-checkpoint FAIL line.

Resolves #40529

title: t19419: refactor(pulse): run the LLM supervisor in its own lane and remove the drain-escape layers
body:
## Summary

The LLM supervisor no longer runs on the cycle tail. After a full cycle (drained or not) releases the instance lock and hands off its census, it wakes a detached one-shot pulse-wrapper.sh --supervisor-lane=<full|degraded> (systemd user service on Linux, setsid nohup otherwise, as with the GH#38696 refill wake) and exits. The cycle-owned routines ticker wakes a queue-trigger-only lane at most every PULSE_SUPERVISOR_LANE_TICK_SECONDS (default 900, 0 disables). The lane takes no instance or dispatch lock, yields to any live LLM-lock holder (one session per runner, including an older bundle's in-cycle supervisor), skips during runtime transitions and the stop flag, uses its own pid file (pulse-supervisor-lane.pid) and never runs the early-exit recycle dispatch. A drained earlier-bundle cycle wakes the activated bundle's lane. Removed: the GH#38162 drain escape, GH#38210 deferral marker and GH#38580 backstop (_pulse_defer_drain_supervisor_escape and the marker helpers, PULSE_LLM_DRAIN_ESCAPE_SECONDS/_DEFER/_MAX_DEFER_SECONDS); a leftover marker is deleted. The GH#34000 degraded-prefetch escape stays. Rollback: PULSE_SUPERVISOR_LANE=0 restores in-cycle execution with a plain GH#37907 drain skip. Known trade-offs: cycles now run during sessions, so the supervisor watchdog's pulse.log growth check can be masked (as GH#38696 refill runs already do; wall-clock and idle timeouts still bound it), and pulse.pid stays IDLE while a lane session runs. Decision record: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/40536#issuecomment-7207635656



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-routines-tick.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-supervisor-starvation-escape.sh

Verifier: deploy, then confirm in pulse.log a 'Supervisor lane: waking mode=full source=cycle' line per cycle, a lane 'evaluating' line, an 'LLM supervisor attempt started' from the lane PID while later cycles keep starting, no 'starvation escape'/'deferring' lines on drained cycles, and pulse-wrapper.log 'wake skipped (LLM session already running' while a session runs.
